report.text: UPL Matchweek 1
Mohawk City 1 - 0 Spindles
An exciting weekend for the Spins turned into a disappointing one after a 1-0 loss to Mohawk City FC in our first ever UPL match.
The UPL kicked off on May 17, with 6 different clubs competing all across the Capital Region.
Spindles United proudly co-founded the UPL and have helped get the league to a Matchweek 1.
Despite a successful kickoff weekend across the league, Spindles would unfortunately not have much to celebrate.
Spindles travelled away for Matchweek 1 to Union College to Mohawk City FC
The match did not offer much from either side.
Midfield battles lost and won by both teams, with a handful of chances at both ends.

In the 22nd minute of the match Spindles were awarded a corner kick from which Mohawk countered and some sloppy defensive play from Spindles lead to the first and only goal of the match from Mohawk city.
After a poor first half Spindles came out in the second with more build up play and chances on goal.
However, no one was able to break the deadlock.
A game full of emotions lead defender Nico Faretta to receive his second yellow card in his Spindles debut and Spindles were down to 10 men with 5 minutes left to play.
Spindles pushed but could not find the net.
The match ended 1-0 to Mohawk city, handing Spindles their first loss ever in a season opening match.
Spindles will look to bounce back and get their first goal and first win next week with a much anticipated match up with a cross river rival Collar City FC
That match will be played on Friday May 22nd 7pm at Lansingburgh High School.

report.text: Collar City FC 1 - 0 Spindles
Spindles United (0-1) made the trip across the Hudson River to face Collar City FC (1-0) in their first scheduled UPL match after years of competing in the CDSL.

As expected, the match was a hard-fought battle from the opening whistle. Spindles started brightly, applying pressure to Collar City’s backline and creating several promising opportunities early on, but were unable to find the breakthrough.
The intensity and quality of the match continued to grow throughout the first half, with both sides remaining organized defensively as the game entered halftime scoreless at 0-0.

Collar City looked dangerous on the counterattack throughout the second half, testing the Spindles defense with quick transitions and direct play. At the other end, Spindles continued to create chances but could not convert their opportunities into goals.

The decisive moment came in the 75th minute when Collar City capitalized on a counterattack. A long ball over the top split the defense, allowing the forward to race through, round the Spindles goalkeeper, and calmly finish to give the hosts a 1-0 lead, 75’.
Spindles pushed forward in search of an equalizer during the closing stages, but despite creating additional chances, the final touch continued to evade them.
Collar City earned a red card in the 90’, but the man advantage didn’t last long.
The match remained physical and competitive until the final whistle, with Collar City securing the 1-0 victory.
Spindles United (0-2) will now turn their attention to Friday, May 30, when they host Patroon United (2-0) in the club’s first-ever competitive home match at Waterford-Halfmoon High School.

report.text: Spindles 1 - 0 Patroon
35’ - Kankam (Trestick)
Spindles United (0-2) welcomed Patroon United (2-0) for a highly competitive UPL fixture and the club’s first-ever competitive home match.
More than 150 people showed out to our first home match at the Waterford Turf Field & Track. A beautiful complex that we are grateful to the school district for allowing use this year.

After a difficult start to the season, Spindles were determined to turn the page in front of their home supporters. The match opened at a frantic pace, with both sides battling for control. Spindles held the early advantage, creating several promising opportunities, but once again struggled to find the finishing touch.
That changed midway through the first half.

After absorbing pressure, Spindles launched a quick counterattack. The ball found Anders Trestick, who burst forward on a dazzling 40-yard run before delivering a perfectly weighted pass across the box. Waiting at the far post was David Kankam, who calmly slotted home to score both his first goal of the season and the first UPL goal in club history, giving Spindles a 1-0 lead, 35’.
The intensity continued to rise as both teams exchanged chances, but Spindles carried their advantage into halftime.

Patroon emerged from the break with renewed energy, pressing higher and committing numbers forward in search of an equalizer. Both clubs knew how important the three points would be, and every challenge reflected it.
The match took a dramatic turn early in the second half when a Spindles defender was shown a straight red card following a tackle, reducing the hosts to 10 men.
Spindles reorganized and dug in defensively, but the adversity was not over.

Minutes later, a Patroon counterattack forced the Spindles goalkeeper into a desperate challenge outside the box. Following a collision and handball, the referee produced a second red card, leaving Spindles with just nine players on the field.
With no substitute goalkeeper available, captain Marcos Lopez stepped up and volunteered to take his place between the posts.
Facing a two-man disadvantage and a midfielder in net, Spindles knew it would take a complete team effort to see out the result.

What followed was a remarkable display of resilience, discipline, and determination. Every player committed fully to the defensive effort, covering ground, winning tackles, and putting their bodies on the line to protect the lead.
Despite being down two players, Spindles remained dangerous on the counterattack and came close to extending their advantage on several occasions.
Patroon threw everything forward in the closing stages, but Spindles refused to break.
When the final whistle sounded, the home crowd erupted as Spindles secured a hard-fought 1-0 victory, earning the club’s first win of the season and first competitive home victory.
New addition Ethan Valente was named Man of the Match after an outstanding performance, showcasing an incredible work rate and rising to the demands of a fiercely contested match.
Spindles United (1-2) will look to build on the momentum next week when they return home to face United Soccer Group (0-2).

report.text: Spindles 1 - 0 USG
18’ - Locicero (P)
Spindles United FC Earn Hard-Fought 1-0 Victory Over United Soccer Group

WATERFORD, N.Y. — Spindles United FC (2-0-2) hosted United Soccer Group (USG) (1-1-2) on Sunday evening at Waterford-Halfmoon Turf, with both sides entering the match looking to improve to 2-0-2 on the season.
The match also marked a milestone for the club as Spindles United held its first-ever live stream, featuring commentary from Ben Kellis and Papa Ndiaye. Fans can watch the full match replay here.

The veteran Spindles side faced a youthful and energetic USG squad, and it was the home team that looked the more dangerous side early. Spindles controlled much of the possession in the opening stages and created several promising attacking opportunities.

The breakthrough came in the 18th minute. Ethan Valente collected the ball and glided through the USG defense before attempting to round the goalkeeper. The USG keeper brought Valente down inside the penalty area, earning Spindles a penalty kick.

Captain John Locicero stepped up and confidently buried his effort into the top corner, giving Spindles a 1-0 lead. The goal marked another historic moment for the club, as Locicero recorded his 20th career goal for Spindles United FC, extending his record as the club’s all-time leading scorer.
The remainder of the first half saw chances for both sides, with Spindles continuing to threaten in attack but unable to add to their advantage. The home side entered halftime leading 1-0.

USG emerged from the break with renewed energy, pressing aggressively and looking determined to find an equalizer. The visitors enjoyed extended spells of possession throughout the second half and generated several dangerous attacking moments.

Despite the pressure, Spindles once again delivered a disciplined defensive performance. The back line remained organized, dealing effectively with USG’s direct play and limiting quality scoring opportunities.

The match continued to go back and forth throughout the final 45 minutes, but neither side could find another breakthrough. Spindles ultimately held firm to secure a 1-0 victory and their second clean sheet of the season.
For his match-winning goal and overall attacking impact, John Locicero was named Man of the Match.
Thanks to all the supporters that joined us in-person despite the pre-match weather!
And a special thanks to all the volunteers on the day.

Spindles United FC now turns its attention to a tough road test on Sunday, June 14th, when they travel to Dockstader Recreational Park in Galway, New York, to take on the Sacandaga Lakers (2-0-2). Kickoff is scheduled for 2:30 p.m.

report.text: Sacandaga 2 - 3 Spindles
21’ - Adjei (Valente)
77’ - Trestick (Ad. Singaporewala)
88’ - Palumbo
June 14, 2026 | Galway, NY
Spindles United FC (2-0-2) traveled to Galway on Sunday afternoon to take on the Sacandaga Lakers (2-0-2) in a crucial Upstate Premier League matchup.

The match began at a high tempo, with both sides battling for control of possession. Spindles settled into the game quickly and controlled much of the early play, creating several dangerous opportunities in the attacking third. A breakthrough goal felt inevitable.

That breakthrough arrived in the 21’. After winning possession near midfield, Spindles worked the ball to Ethan Valente, who found Zeidane Adeji in space. Adeji unleashed a stunning strike from 30 yards out that rocketed past the goalkeeper and into the back of the net for his first goal of the season, giving Spindles a deserved 1-0 lead.
Spindles continued to push for a second goal before halftime, but the Lakers remained organized defensively and kept the deficit at one.

As the first half progressed, Sacandaga began to grow into the match. Utilizing direct play, long throws, and dangerous set pieces, the Lakers consistently tested the Spindles defense. Their persistence paid off in the 44’ when a well-driven corner kick found an unmarked attacker inside the box, who finished first-time to level the match at 1-1 heading into halftime.

The intensity only increased after the break. Spindles once again controlled the majority of possession and looked to press high up the field, while Sacandaga searched for opportunities to play direct balls behind the back line. Both teams created quality chances, but neither could find the decisive touch.

The deadlock was finally broken in the 77’. Midfielder Adam Singaporewala won a hard-fought challenge, maintained possession, and slipped a weighted through ball to Anders Trestick. Trestick beat his defender and calmly placed his finish into the bottom corner for his first goal of the season, restoring Spindles’ lead at 2-1.
The lead, however, would not last long.

Just three minutes later, Sacandaga earned another corner kick after threatening from set pieces throughout the afternoon. A quality delivery found the head of a Lakers attacker, who powered home the equalizer to make it 2-2 in the 81’.
With time winding down, both teams pushed for a winner. The match opened up into an end-to-end battle as each side searched for all three points.

In the 88’, Spindles earned a free kick in a dangerous shooting position just outside the box. With the game hanging in the balance, Frankie Palumbo stepped up to take the set piece. Under immense pressure, Palumbo delivered in spectacular fashion, curling his effort into the bottom corner to give Spindles a dramatic 3-2 lead in the dying moments.
The Lakers threw everything forward during stoppage time, but the Spindles defense responded with crucial tackles, clearances, and relentless determination to preserve the advantage.
When the final whistle sounded, Spindles had secured a thrilling 3-2 victory.
Zeidane Adjei earned the Man of the Match award for his opening goal, easily a contender for Goal of the Season.
The win marks Spindles’ third consecutive victory and improves their record to 3-0-2 on the season, moving them into second place in the UPL standings at the midway point of the campaign.
Up Next:
Spindles United FC return home Friday, June 19, to face Mohawk City FC (3-0-2) at Waterford-Halfmoon Turf. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:15 PM in what promises to be a key matchup between the two sides.

Spindles United (3-0-2) welcomed fellow Upstate Premier League contender Mohawk City FC (3-0-2) to Waterford-Halfmoon High School for a pivotal Matchweek 6 clash.

The opening 45 minutes were evenly contested, with both sides battling for possession and neither able to create many clear-cut opportunities. Spindles began to settle into the match as halftime approached, controlling much of the ball but unable to find the breakthrough as the teams entered the break level at 0-0.

The hosts came out with purpose in the second half, and their pressure was rewarded in the 51st minute. A well-worked team move found John Locicero on the wing, who delivered a dangerous ball into the box. Zeidane Adjei met it first time with his weaker foot, firing home to give Spindles a deserved 1-0 lead and net his second goal of the UPL season.

The advantage, however, was short-lived. Mohawk City responded by raising the intensity and eventually found an equalizer in the 64th minute. A swift counterattack ended with a pinpoint cross and a perfectly placed header to level the score at 1-1.

The visitors continued to press, and with emotions running high, they completed the comeback in the 70th minute. Another dangerous ball across the face of goal found its target, with Mohawk calmly finishing from close range to take a 2-1 lead.

Spindles searched for a late response, but Mohawk’s defense stood firm through the closing stages. Despite a strong start to the second half, the hosts were unable to recover as they dropped all three points at home.

report.text: Patroon 1 - 4 Spindles
1’ - Trestick
80’ - Trestick (Locicero)
83’ - Trestick
88’ - Breen (Sanchez)
July 12, 2026 | Colonie, NY

With playoff positioning becoming increasingly important, Spindles United traveled to face Patroon United in the second meeting between the two clubs this season. The first encounter ended in a gritty 1-0 Spindles victory despite playing down two men. This time, however, Spindles arrived at full strength, and they wasted no time making their presence felt.

Just 17 seconds into the match, Spindles struck. An aggressive high press from the front two forced a mistake from the Patroon goalkeeper, whose misplaced pass fell straight to Anders Trestick. Without hesitation, Trestick unleashed a first-time finish into the back of the net, scoring the fastest goal in Spindles United history and giving the visitors an instant 1-0 lead. 1-0, 1’.

The early goal set the tone for a competitive first half. Both sides battled for control in midfield, with Patroon searching for long balls over the top while Spindles’ back line stood firm. Chances came at both ends, but disciplined defending and solid goalkeeping kept the score unchanged as Spindles carried a 1-0 advantage into halftime.

The second half continued with both teams searching for the next breakthrough. Patroon found their opportunity after a Spindles foul created a dangerous free-kick just outside the area. The ensuing strike slipped through the wall and nestled into the back of the net, leveling the match at 1-1.
Rather than panic, Spindles remained composed. They controlled stretches of possession and created several promising attacks, but the finishing touch remained elusive.
That changed in the 80th minute.

A brilliant individual effort from John Locicero saw him beat his defender down the wing before cutting inside and forcing a strong save from the Patroon goalkeeper. Waiting in the perfect position was Anders Trestick, who hammered the rebound into the top corner with his left foot to restore the Spindles lead. The finish completed Trestick’s brace and put Spindles ahead 2-1, 80’.

Only three minutes later, Trestick wasn’t finished. Relentless pressing forced another turnover deep in Patroon’s half, allowing him to race in one-on-one with the goalkeeper. Calmly slotting home the finish, Trestick completed a remarkable hat trick, bringing his UPL tally to four goals and extending the lead to 3-1, 83’.

Spindles continued to push forward, looking to put the match beyond doubt. Following an extended spell of possession, Danny Sanchez picked out Ryan Breen in space. Breen drove directly at the Patroon defense, split two defenders with a brilliant run, and unleashed a thunderous strike from 25 yards that rocketed into the net for his first UPL goal of the season. It was a spectacular finish that capped off a dominant closing stretch for the visitors. 4-1, 88’.
Spindles comfortably saw out the remaining minutes, turning in another outstanding defensive performance to secure a convincing 4-1 victory on the road.
The win improves Spindles United to 4-1-3, strengthening their push toward a UPL playoff berth, while Patroon United falls to 4-2-2.

With the postseason race heating up, Spindles will look to build on their momentum next week when they take on United Soccer Group (3-1-4). Man of the Match honors went to Anders Trestick after his second career Spindles hat trick, highlighted by the fastest goal in club history just 17 seconds into the match.
Up Next:
Spindles United FC are back on the road on Friday night at Afrim’s Sports Park to take on 2-win streak United Soccer Group.

July 17, 2026 | Albany, NY
With the race for the first-ever UPL playoffs heating up, Spindles United traveled to take on United Soccer Group in a crucial matchup between two teams battling for a spot in the postseason.

From the opening whistle, the match was played at a high pace, with both sides looking to take control. USG worked to move the ball around the pitch and break down the Spindles backline, but the visitors stood strong and refused to give their opponents any easy opportunities.
As the match progressed, Spindles began to take control of possession and create chances of their own.

In the 22nd minute, Spindles earned their first truly dangerous opportunity from a corner kick. Frankie Palumbo delivered a dangerous ball into the box, creating chaos as multiple Spindles players battled to get a touch. The ball eventually fell to Anders Trestick just inside the 18-yard box. Trestick calmly set himself up and placed his shot into the bottom corner to give Spindles the lead. 1-0, 22’.
The goal marked Trestick’s fifth UPL goal of the season.
The momentum continued to favor the visitors, who maintained possession and continued to put pressure on the USG defense. Then, in the 41st minute, Spindles doubled their advantage.

A free kick from roughly 40 yards out presented another opportunity. Mason Kievit delivered a perfectly placed ball over the USG defense, finding a crashing Captain Marcos Lopez, who finished the chance to score his first UPL goal of the season. 2-0, 41’.
The second half was different for the Spins.
Spindles continued to control much of the possession coming out of the break, but USG refused to go quietly.
The final 15 minutes saw the momentum shift dramatically.

USG began throwing numbers forward and creating dangerous chances. A cutting USG winger fired a shot toward the Spindles goal that was saved by the Spindles goalkeeper. The ball, however, nearly crossed the line, and despite a desperate attempt by a Spindles defender to clear the danger, the ball ultimately found its way into the net. 2-1.
Moments later, USG struck again.
A ball was played in behind the Spindles center backs and collected by the USG striker, who calmly chipped the Spindles goalkeeper to bring the match level. 2-2.
With everything to play for and three crucial points on the line, both teams continued to battle for a late winner. Chances came at both ends, but neither defense would break again.
After a dramatic final stretch, the match ended 2-2.
The result moves Spindles United to 4-2-3 with 14 points, as the club enters the final week of the inaugural UPL season still fighting for a place in the first-ever playoffs.
Spindles will close out the regular season at home on Sunday, July 26, when they welcome the Sacandaga Lakers (3-1-5) to Waterford-Halfmoon Turf.
With the playoffs on the line, there is still everything to play for.

report.text: Spindles 5 - 0 Sacandaga
15’ - Rabadi (Plumley)

65’ - Rabadi (Trestick)

Waterford, NY — July 26, 2026
Spindles United entered Sunday night’s matchup with everything to play for.

Sitting at 4-2-3, Spindles welcomed the Sacandaga Lakers (3-1-5) to Waterford-Halfmoon in a highly anticipated UPL matchup. With the regular season winding down, Spindles were looking to improve their playoff position, while Sacandaga entered the night fighting to secure their place in the postseason.
By the final whistle, Spindles had made a statement.
Five goals. A clean sheet. And first place in the UPL.

The match began with Spindles taking control of possession, moving the ball with purpose and looking to dictate the tempo. Sacandaga dropped into a defensive shape, hoping to absorb the pressure and create opportunities on the counterattack.
After several early chances narrowly missed the final touch, Spindles finally broke through in the 15th minute.

A shot from Ty Plumley deflected off a Sacandaga defender, sending the ball directly into the path of Matt Rabadi just outside the 18-yard box. Rabadi took an excellent first touch to set himself up before calmly slotting the ball past the keeper and into the bottom corner. 1-0, 15’.
The goal marked Rabadi’s second of the season and gave Spindles the early advantage.

The remainder of the first half followed a similar script. Spindles controlled possession and continued to probe for openings, but the Sacandaga defense and goalkeeper stood tall, keeping the Lakers within striking distance.
Spindles carried their 1-0 lead into halftime.
Coming out of the break, Spindles looked to continue where they left off — controlling possession, breaking down the Sacandaga defense and creating chances in the final third.
The chances continued to come, but Spindles struggled to find the finishing touch.
That changed in the 61st minute.

A high press from Anders Trestick forced a mistake on a Sacandaga backpass, with the goalkeeper sending a wayward ball directly into the path of Ryan Breen. Breen quickly took advantage, winning possession before shifting the ball onto his left foot and calmly finishing to double the Spindles lead. 2-0, 61’.
It was Breen’s second UPL goal of the season.
The second goal only seemed to fuel Spindles further.

Just four minutes later, in the 65th minute, some excellent combination play found Trestick in space. The midfielder delivered an incisive pass between two Sacandaga defenders, perfectly picking out the darting run of Rabadi.
Rabadi found himself one-on-one with the goalkeeper and made no mistake.
He calmly slotted the ball home for his second goal of the night, completing his brace and giving Spindles a commanding 3-0 lead. 3-0, 65’.
Rabadi’s second goal brought his total to three UPL goals on the season.
Spindles continued to push forward as the game entered its final stages, and in the 82nd minute, they struck again.

On the counterattack, John Locicero received the ball deep in the middle third. Rather than slowing the attack down, Locicero delivered a perfectly weighted cross-field through ball, splitting multiple defenders and finding Trestick in stride.
Trestick carried the ball into the box before calmly placing his shot into the bottom corner. 4-0, 82’.
The goal marked Trestick’s sixth UPL goal of the season, adding another tally to an already impressive campaign.
But Spindles still weren’t finished.

With the Lakers struggling to contain the attack, more chances continued to fall the hosts’ way. In the 89th minute, Spindles once again controlled possession and worked the ball forward to Daniel Primeau.
Primeau cut inside before finding Zeidane Adjei, who appeared to be in an offside position. However, a Sacandaga defender had kept Adjei onside, allowing play to continue.
Adjei made no mistake.
He buried the opportunity to make it five. 5-0, 89’.
The final whistle soon followed, sealing a dominant victory for the hosts.
Spindles United finished the regular season with a 5-2-3 record, scoring 18 goals while conceding just 10, good for a +8 goal difference.
But the biggest result of the night came away from Waterford-Halfmoon.
After United Soccer Group and Patroon United played to a 3-3 draw, Spindles United officially moved to the top of the UPL table, securing first place heading into the playoffs.
The regular season is over.
Now, the real work begins.
Man of the Match: Matt Rabadi — Rabadi controlled the midfield and stamped his authority on the game with a brace, helping lead Spindles to a dominant 5-0 victory.

Albany, NY — August 2, 2026
Rabadi, Locicero find the net as No. 1 seed Spindles shut out USG and punch their ticket to the championship.
Spindles United is heading back to a league final.
The top-seeded Spindles defeated No. 4 seed United Soccer Group, 2-0, in a hard-fought UPL semifinal Sunday, advancing to the league championship and keeping their hopes of another trophy alive.
USG controlled possession early, but Spindles gradually settled into the match and began finding opportunities.
The breakthrough came in the 22nd minute.

After USG turned the ball over deep in Spindles territory, Anders Trestick quickly found Nico Faretta with a diagonal pass. Faretta drove at the defense before slipping the ball to Matt Rabadi, who took a touch and buried a shot into the bottom corner. 1-0, 22’.
Rabadi’s fourth goal of the season. 1-0, 22’.
Spindles wouldn’t have to wait long for another.
USG earned a dangerous set piece in the Spindles defensive third, but Captain Dan Crook rose to clear the ball out of the box. Matt Rabadi collected it and quickly moved the ball to Faretta.
Faretta then floated a beautiful ball over the USG backline to Trestick.
Trestick raced to the byline and cut the ball back to a trailing Captain John Locicero, who calmly finished into the corner.
Locicero’s 2nd on the season 2-0 Spindles. 2-0, 32’.
Both goals came on the counter, as Spindles repeatedly punished USG when opportunities opened up in transition.
Spindles carried the two-goal advantage into halftime, but the job was far from finished.
USG came out looking to find a way back into the match, creating chances and continuing to battle for possession. But the Spindles defense refused to crack.
Ryan Taylor came up with several acrobatic saves to preserve the clean sheet, while the backline consistently dealt with USG’s attempts to get in behind.
The final minutes belonged to Spindles, who remained disciplined and composed as the clock wound down.
Then came the final whistle.
Spindles United 2, United Soccer Group 0.
And Spindles are going to the UPL Final.
After the Spins match, Patroon United punched its ticket to the championship with a 2-1 victory over Mohawk City FC. Setting up a matchup between the league’s top two seeds.

No. 1 Spindles United (6-2-3) vs. No. 2 Patroon United (5-4-2)
August 9, 2026 — 6:00 PM
Christian Pulmeri Sports Complex
For Spindles, the opportunity is familiar — but the league is new.
After winning the CDSL championship last season, Spindles have reached a league final in consecutive years, this time in the inaugural UPL season.
One more win would give the club its second straight league championship and its first UPL trophy.
MAN OF THE MATCH — LUCA GRESTINI

Grestini was a force defensively, playing with a relentless motor throughout the semifinal. He consistently stepped into challenges, disrupted USG’s attack and helped anchor a Spindles backline that finished the night with a clean sheet.
One final stands between Spindles and another trophy.

Albany, NY – August 9, 2026
Rabadi and Trestick score, Crook leads the defense as Spindles shut out Patroon 2-0 to make history in Albany
One year after winning the CDSL for the first time, Spindles United have got their hands on another trophy.
This time, they’re the first.

Spindles United defeated Patroon United 2-0 on Sunday at the Christian Plumeri Sports Complex on Sullivan Field, capturing the inaugural Upstate Premier League championship in front of more than 300 fans.
The top-seeded Spindles came in at 6-2-3, facing a Patroon side that finished second at 5-4-2. Ninety minutes later, Spindles had made league history.
Spindles controlled the early possession, looking to play through Patroon’s pressure and dictate the tempo.
Patroon’s defense held firm through the opening half hour.
Then came the breakthrough.
In the 35th minute, Spindles won the ball deep in Patroon territory. After a battle for possession, the ball found veteran Daniel Primeau, who immediately looked toward the back post.
Primeau delivered, Matt Rabadi was waiting.
The Spindles midfielder met the ball with a perfectly timed volley and buried it. 1-0, 35’.
It was Rabadi’s fifth goal of the UPL season, his second in playoffs and the biggest one yet.
Patroon tried to respond before halftime, but Ryan Taylor and the Spindles back line refused to give up an equalizer.
Spindles took the 1-0 lead into the break.
Patroon came out of halftime with urgency.
The pressure increased. The press got higher.
Spindles kept playing.
And in the 51st minute, they found the goal that changed the game.
After a strong possession sequence, Nico Faretta picked up the ball and saw the opening. He threaded a pass straight through the Patroon defense.

Anders Trestick was in. Trestick took a few touches under pressure before moving the ball onto his left foot. Then he finished. The shot slipped through the goalkeeper’s legs and into the net. 2-0, 51’.
Trestick’s seventh goal of the UPL campaign gave Spindles a two-goal cushion with nearly 40 minutes still to play.
Patroon wasn’t going away however.
The second seed continued to push forward, holding possession for stretches and creating opportunities.
But Spindles had answers.
Taylor stood tall in goal. The back line absorbed the pressure. And in the middle of it all was captain Dan Crook.
Crook seemed to be everywhere.
Every loose ball. Every dangerous attack. Every moment when Patroon threatened to pull one back. The oldest player on the pitch was there.
Spindles kept Patroon off the scoreboard.
At the other end, Spindles had opportunities to put the final completely out of reach, but the two-goal lead was enough.
The clock kept moving.
90 minutes.
Then the whistle.
Spindles United 2. Patroon United 0.
HISTORY MADE
Spindles United are the first-ever UPL champions.
The club’s championship run is even more impressive considering how the season began.
Spindles opened the campaign 0-2. However they didn’t panic. They battled back, climbed the table, finished first at 7-2-3, scored 22 goals and conceded only 10.
Now they have back-to-back league championships.
2025: CDSL Champions.
2026: UPL Champions.
Different league. Different challenge. Same ending.
Spindles players lifted the inaugural UPL trophy in front of a UPL record attendance crowd (286) that had come to watch history.
They got exactly that.
MAN OF THE MATCH: DAN CROOK
The Spindles captain delivered when it mattered most.
Crook anchored the defense, cleaned up dangerous chances and provided the leadership that helped Spindles preserve the clean sheet.
The championship may have been won with goals from Rabadi and Trestick.
But it was finished by a defense led by its captain.
Dan Crook. Man of the Match.
Spindles United. Inaugural UPL Champions.
Spindles played in a crucial role in operations of the Inaugural UPL Season. Despite a successful campaign all across the league, there is a ton of work that has to be done to improve.
2026 was only an experiment. One that we learned a lot from that will help propel the league to a completely new stage in 2027, and raising the standards of amateur football in the area.
We can’t wait.

On Thursday night, Spindles kicked off the 2025 CDSL campaign with an emphatic victory over our across the bridge rivals Collar City FC.
A beautiful night to return to Nott Road for a 4th year straight, Spindles wasted no time getting on the score sheet.
In the 5th minute, an easy pass from Spindles Captain Marcos Lopez gave Zeidane Adjei time and space to cut inside with his right, and power one into the top left corner from outside the 18. 1-0, 5’.
Spindles continued to press, putting pressure on the Collar City backline.
10 minutes later, Lopez takes a shot inside the box before hitting the hand of a City defender.
Penalty to Spindles, as John Locicero buried it home in the top corner. 2-0, 15’.
More pressure from Spindles in the first half gave a free kick to Mason Kievit from half.
Kievit whipped one in to find Jimmy Alexander who brought it down and squared it across for an easy tap-in by Captain Dan Crook. 3-0, 31’.
Before finishing the half, Spindles look to create one last chance. Lopez fed a simple pass again to Ammar Singaporewala who sent a left foot curler near post. His first ever Spindles goal. 4-0, 45’.
Spirits were high at half-time. And Spindles wanted to keep the party going in the second.
1 minute after the second kickoff, Locicero pressured the back line forcing error by defender and keeper opening the net for his second of the night. 5-0, 47’.
Less than 10 minutes later, Collar City would look to get one back with a right foot curler. 5-1, 55’.
However, that is where their night on the scoresheet would end.
Some good build up play by the Spindles midfield saw Andrew Michel give an easy pass to Singaporewala, who sent a knuckling shot from 30 yards over the keeper. His second of the night. 6-1, 81’.

The scoresheet was capped off in the dying minutes, when Locicero sent a thread pass through the middle to Anders Trestick on his Spindles debut. Trestick took it past the last defender, before tucking it around the keeper for his first Spindles goal. 7-1, 91’.
The final whistle blew, capping off a huge scoreline for our season opener.
Ammar Singaporewala was named the Bear Digital Man of the Match for his 2 goals, and dominance of the midfield from minute 1 to 90.
Club Records
This win marked a handful of club records.
Most goals scored in a single match (7) (Previously 6 against Collar City FC in 2023, formerly known as Backheel FC).
Largest victory margin (6) (Previously 5 against Collar City FC in 2023, formerly known as Backheel FC).
Now 4/4 wins in our opening match, since the club was founded in 2022 (Highlanders, 2022. Highlanders, 2023. Ligon FC, 2024. Collar City FC, 2025).
Club Debuts
Spindles also saw 5 new players make their club debut in Thursday nights match.
Anders Trestick
Adam Singaporewala
Josh Donner
Lucas Nathan
Manuel Zevallos
We wish Josh Donner luck on his recovery from injury.

After a rainy week, the skies cleared for our Tuesday night matchup against 2024 CDSL Champions, FCSB.
An entertaining game for the neutral, saw Spindles take all 3 points in the end.
The match kicked off with Spindles on their heels for a majority of the first half.
As expected, FCSB are a top side who came to score. However, the Spindles backline led by Captain Dan Crook stayed strong for the entire first half.
Goal line clearances, last ditch tackles and big saves from goalkeeper Ryan Taylor kept both sides level at 0-0. End of the first half.
The second half started, and FCSB continued to press for that opening goal.
As the game became more stretched, some high press from Spindles saw the FCSB keeper and defense miscommunicate, leaving Anders Trestick to run past both and tap one home in an open net.
Against the wave of play, Spindles open the scoring. 1-0, 47’.
FCSB continued to press, leaving plenty of work for the Spindles backline.
However, after about 10 minutes a corner kick found the head of an FCSB player. 1-1, 55’.
Shortly after, another chance found the champs in behind the line and easily putting another away. 1-2, 60’.
The pressure continued to pile on Spindles, now trailing 2-1. However, the chances started coming on both ends now.
With less than 10 minutes to go, a shot by Zeidane Adjei goes straight into the hand of an FCSB defender, which is outstretched over his head. Penalty to Spindles.
Adjei calmly steps up, and buries it home bottom left corner. 2-2, 84’.
In a game of drama, it was looking more and more like both sides would share the spoils.
However in the dying minutes of the match, Adjei breaks away down the right side before being taken out by an FCSB defender just inside the penalty area. Another penalty to Spindles.
Despite FCSB’s cries that the foul was not on the box, the referee proceeded to hand out a red card to one of their defenders for verbal abuse.

The last minute of the game, rightfully so Adjei steps up for another chance. This time to steal all 3 points. And that is just what he did. Slotted away in the bottom right corner just under the keeper. 3-2, 90’.
After a few minutes of additional time, the referee blew the final whistle sealing the win for the Spins.
Handing FCSB their first loss (in a regulation game) since they rejoined the league in 2024.
Spindles saw some big performances from everyone, especially in the back two-thirds.
However, Adjei took on the pressure and converted the game tying goal, and game winner from the spot. Earning him the Guth DeConzo Man of the Match award.
Special thank you to all the supporters who made it out on Tuesday night!
Spindles return to action on Sunday afternoon at 3 pm, where we will take on Highlanders and hope to go 4-0 on the season.

report.text: Spindles 3 - 2 FCSB (OT)

We wanted to start by apologizing to anyone who missed Tuesday night’s spectacle at Nott Road.
An overtime thriller between two heavyweight sides gave all spectators a match to remember.
On Tuesday night, 2nd seed Spindles United took on 3rd seed, and 2024 Champions FCSB in the CDSL semi-final.
The winner would book a spot in the 2025 CDSL final.
The Spins met FCSB once earlier this season, where they secured a 3-2 victory thanks to two last minute penalties by Zeidane Adjei.
Spindles knew it was going to be their toughest test since joining the league. And that it would take a lot of work and preparation, with a little bit of magic to take them down.
Despite the near heat-advisory temperatures, the match kicked off with high energy.
A few chances fell to Spindles on the counter-attack in the first half. But as expected, Spindles focused on defense from the start.
20 minutes in, a reckless challenge from an FCSB defender ended the season for our own Josh Donner. We wish him a speedy recovery!
FCSB tried to break the Spindles backline, but captains Marcos Lopez, Dan Crook and Goalkeeper Ryan Taylor kept Spindles in check.
The half ended 0-0, all the play for.
The second half brought similar energy from the start. With both sides battling in the midfield for possession.
Unfortunately, a defensive lapse 20 minutes in saw FCSB in on goal to open the scoring. 1-0, FCSB, 70’.
A tough blow for a strong defensive performance by the Spins.
However, the energy was not gone.
FCSB pushed for a second, but Spindles took advantage of their subs to find an equalizer.
Just as things began to look bleak for the Spins, a well worked attack found David Kankam on the wing.
A deflected 50/50 between him and the FCSB defender popped up in the box. Jimmy Alexander took it down and hit it low across the keeper. The players and crowd erupt. 1-1, 86’.
Spindles stay alive in their hopes to get to the final.
Regulation ended 1-1.
As we neared sundown, the referees turned on the Nott Road lights to mark Spindles first night game of the season.
By CDSL rules, we entered into 2-10 minute halves of extra time to decide the winner before penalties.
And the magic continued into extra-time.
Shortly after the kickoff, a corner kick by Lewis Whalen caused a jumble between 3 FCSB defenders.
One of their headers popped the ball up to the penalty spot where Crook hit a weak-foot volley to the far left post.
Crook celebrates with madness, and Spindles are ahead for the first time on the night. 1 step closer to the final. 2-1, 92’.
Spindles looked to be in control as the first half of extra-time came to a close.
The second half kicked off, 10 minutes away from the CDSL final.
FCSB pressed for an equalizer.
Goalkeeper Ryan Taylor kept Spindles in the game time and time again. Big saves left and right to stop the highest scoring players in the leagues history.
Early into the second half, FCSB win a corner.
The cross comes towards the Spindles keeper, where he was controversially taken down as he attempted to punch the ball away. Leaving an open header for FCSB. Their equalizer, 2-2, 103’.
At that point, both teams are running on fumes.
The match was surely headed to penalties.
Ian Maguire finds himself pressing on the wing, winning a foul for the Spins near the spectator side corner.
Our equalizing goalscorer, Alexander steps over the freekick.
*Referee blows his whistle*
Alexander whips one in back post. Crook is covered by two defenders.
Thats when John Locicero screamed, rose over the defenders and headed the cross down and past the goalkeeper. Spindles go nuts. 3-2, 108’.
Locicero runs to the corner to celebrate with the whole team who are going mad.
2 minutes later, the final whistle was blown. Marking Locicero’s goal as the over-time game winner that sent Spindles to their 2nd CDSL final.
A spectacle at Nott Road, to say the least. Cinema.
More than 100 people attended the match, and witnessed a real showing of Grassroots Football prevailing.
The Spins worked until the final minute, securing a well-deserved victory over a tough opponent. Spindles go 2-1 over FCSB in all-time matchups.
Despite so many great performances for Spindles on Tuesday, midfielder Ammar Singaporewala earned his second Man of the Match award of the season.
Singaporewala was the midfield engine that kept our ship afloat all game. Not coming off the field once in 110 minutes.
The last time Spindles made the CDSL final was in 2023, our second year in the league.
A heart-breaking loss to Vassi Realty set Spindles on a mission to win it all before we take on our next chapter as a club.
Spindles will have another chance at glory this Tuesday, 6:15PM at Nott Road Park. We will play against the winner of Motherland Bros (1) vs. Collar City FC (5).
See y’all there.

matches.reportTitle: Overtime Winner Sends Spindles to their 2nd CDSL Final in 3 years
matches.venueSource: CDSL league venue in club archives

report.text: CDSL FINAL
Spindles 2 - 2 Motherland
(3-1) on Penalties
87’ - Locicero (Breen)
90’ - Lopez (P)
Just when you thought Spindles peaked too early on several occasions this season, they proved otherwise once again.
On Tuesday night, Spindles competed in their second ever CDSL final.
The first one being in the 2023 season, which resulted in a heartbreaking 3-1 loss for the Spins.
But this time, Spindles (2) were coming into a final far more prepared against Motherland Bros (1), a new team to the league that only managed to pick up 1 loss all season long.
Spindles knew this would be their toughest test yet.
Both of our meetings with Motherland this year resulted in losses by 1-goal deficit.
Close games to a team that is blowing out other teams week after week.
It was clear all year long that a Motherland and Spindles final was on the cards for 2025.
The Hurdles
The day kicked off with hurdle after hurdle.
Spindles arrived to Nott Road early to prepare when we noticed the fields were not at all lined for the match.
The CDSL has been dealing with poorly or forgotten lined fields all summer. But it was clear that there was no attention on this one given it was practically invisible.
After a phone call with the town, we learned that our 6:15PM game wasn’t even on their schedule.
Our 6:15PM kickoff was unfortunately pushed to 8:15PM after miscommunication from the CDSL and the Town of Guilderland about the scheduling of this game.
All the fields at Nott Road were being used until 8PM for Pop Warner Football.
Once Pop Warner was finally clear of the fields, allowing us to step on and get ready, another hurdle came when the Town did not send anyone to turn on the lights.
Day-light was moving fast and it was already well past our 8:15PM kickoff.
Eventually they came to turn them on, meaning we finally kicked off by 8:30PM.
The Match
The match kicked off with high intensity from both sides.
Spindles started very defensive, hoping to frustrate the highest scoring team in the CDSL.
Despite the low Spindles block, chances still came our way on the counter-attack.
A run down the wing by Anders Trestick found himself 1-1 with the keeper.
But the tough angle favored the save.
Another chance for John Locicero after a great cross by Ian Maguire, just went wide of the frame.
Motherland dominated the possession and chances in the first half, but Spindles were well and alive. Ending the first half 0-0.
The second half was more of the same.
Spindles created more chances in the first 25, but could not find the back of the net.
Unfortunately, around the 70’, a strong defensive performance by Spindles was hit by a penalty given to Motherland. They easily converted it. 1-0, Motherland, 70’.
A heartbreaking goal that seemed like the end for the Spins.
Chaos on the sidelines due to Motherlands spectators crowding the touchline, along with the substitutes.
Less than 5 minutes later, the pressure continued to pile on as Motherland get another chance. A shot from outside the box beats the Spindles keeper on the near post. 2-0, Motherland, 75’.
The referee begins throwing cards as the kids and spectators began running on the field, knee sliding in celebration of their first CDSL trophy.
Spindles had to be down and out from there.
The Comeback
Time was ticking, and Spindles were running out of time.
Despite transitioning to a more attacking formation, Spindles count not breakdown Motherlands defense anymore.
However, that all changed with 3 minutes left in regulation.
A Hail Mary into the box by Mason Kievit fell to a Motherland defender.
The defender cleared it straight in the air, into Ryan Breen’s path.
Breen crossed it out of the air with his weak foot to the penalty spot where Spindles top score Locicero re-directed it into the right side netting. Spindles have one back, and are alive. 2-1, 87’.
The Spins still had a mountain to climb, hoping for an equalizer with less than 5 minutes left.
Well it wasn’t long before the completed that climb.
In the 90’, a scramble in the box saw Dan Crook go for a header when a Motherland defender swiped at the ball, only to dangerously high kick to Crooks head.

As the whistle blew, the ball fell to Adam Singaporewala who powered the one home into the net. What was surely the equalizer and Singaporewala’s first goal for the club, was taken back as the referee blew his whistle for a penalty before the shot.

After several complaints and a conversation between the AR and Center Ref, it was deemed the whistle to be blown before the shot. Meaning the score remained 2-1, but giving Spindles a chance to equalize from the spot.
Captain Marcos Lopez stepped up, and powered it home into the left side netting. 2-2, 90’.
Spindles were 3 minutes from losing the CDSL final 2-0. And finish regulation 2-2, and are headed into 2, 10 minute halves for overtime. Just like last weeks semi-final.
Simply, Cinema.
Overtime kicked off in Spindles favor. Opportunities started pouring in as the Spins looked to complete the comeback with a win.
It was clear that Spindles depth favored the longer game.
Despite a handful of chances from both sides in over-time, both sides still played timid. Both not wanting to make that defensive mistake to end it all.
Both sides made a handful of substations in light of the inevitable penalty shootout.
OT would end 2-2. Onto our second penalty shootout of the season, after a successful result in the Grassroots Cup.
The Shootout
Spindles shoot first with Breen stepping up to the spot.
And in normal fashion, he doesn’t actually take a step in his shot and just passes it into the bottom right corner. 1-0.
Next, Motherland step up. Goalkeeper Ryan Taylor looks to get into the players head with some antics.
His actions worked as he confidently stopped their first pen, diving to the left. Spindles stay up 1-0.
Captain Lopez steps up, looking to score his second penalty of the game.
With confidence and places it into the right side netting, leaving the keeper in place. 2-0 Spindles.
Motherland look to score their first.
They step up and power one down the middle. Taylor dives but kicks it out with his foot. Huge advantage for Spindles. 2-0.
Spindles look to take a bigger lead. Locicero walks to the spot.
On the whistle he puts his foot through the ball into the bottom left corner. The keeper guesses the right side, but can’t stop the power. 3-0.
Taylor now has the chance to win it all with a save on Motherland for their third penalty.
However, it was clear that they were due, as they put one away in the right side netting. Taylor guesses the spot but can’t get a hand to it. 3-1.
Manu Zevallos steps up to redeem himself from the Grassroots Cup penalty shootout.
With the chance to win it all, Zevallos curls it to the right side. But the Motherland keeper had it covered. 3-1.
Now back into the hands of Taylor.
One save for glory.
Taylor picks the same side for the fourth straight penalty and stops Motherlands low driven shot.
Spindles are complete the comeback and are officially CDSL Champions for the first time.
The Spindles players sprint to Taylor as he flings his arms in the air with glory.
After a season of peaks and valleys, Spindles complete the job in the most dramatic fashion.
No matter what team you supported in this journey, Spindles run had no shortage of entertainment for everyone.
The players celebrated their win lifting the brand new CDSL trophy, hugs all around, and showing gratitude to all their teammates and supporters.
Taylor would be named Man of the Match for his 3 penalty saves during the shootout, including the game-winning save. His first MOTM trophy.
The match would finish around 11:30PM after a match delay, late start, overtime and penalty shootout. Well worth the wait.

Over a hundred people were in attendance supporting Spindles on Tuesday night, with almost 200 people in total there to watch the spectacle. An unsuccessful hate-watch for some, it was surely a final to remember for everyone.
Massive thank you to all supporters, friends, families and sponsors that supported us this season. Though the ups and downs, they were there through it all.
Our CDSL season might be over, but the work for next year starts right away.
Stay tuned for some big changes for Spindles next year.

report.text: Spindles 5 - 1 Ligon
8' - Luke Geczy (Ali Aladlouni)
25' - Ty Plumley (Ian Maguire)
35' - Zeidane Ajdei (Ali Aladlouni)
65' - Joe Piperata (Zeidane Adjei)
85' - Zeidane Adjei (Ammar Singaporewala)
Spindles United's biggest year yet gets off on the right foot with a 5-1 victory on opening night.
It was a perfect evening for Nott Road footy, despite the lack of stadium lighting.
Spindles welcomed CDSL Newcomers Ligon FC with a dominant scoring and possession match.
The Spins opened the scoring within the first 10 minutes.

Picking up right where he left off in last season's semi-final, Luke Geczy got in behind Ligon's defense from a deep threaded pass by Ali Aladlouni. A couple of touches before he slotted it home to the bottom corner. 1 -0, 8'.
Spindles continued to create chances.
Ian Maguire sent wingback Ty Plumley in behind the defense before Plumley touched it around the keeper and put it away—Plumleys first Spindles goal, joining as a new player this season. 2-0, 25'.
Before the break, a mess in the box left Zeidane Ajdei with time and space to put away his first of the season. 3-0, 35'.
Pumped up from a dominant first half, the Spins came out in the second half creating more chances.
Joe Piperata, Russell Sage midfielder who returns to Spindles for the first time since 2022 decided to let one fly from 30 yards.
An unfortunate error from the keeper saw the ball slip into the net. 4-0, 65'.
Despite Spindle's high possession, Ligon did not give up as they continued to look for their opening goal.
A scarp in the box led to Ligon's first goal. 4-1, 73'.
As they looked for a late miracle, that was quickly shut down by a backheel flick by Ammar Singaporewala to put Adjei one-on-one with the keeper. Burying it home. 5-1, 85'.
Adjei would later be named The New Scotland Spirits Man of the Match for his 2 goals and 1 assist.
A great turnout for opening night, with more than 60 supporters showing out.
This win is surely the start Spindles was hoping for as they look to stay undefeated against Highlanders, next week at 8 PM. See you all there.

matches.venueSource: CDSL league venue in club archives

report.text: Highlanders 2 - 1 Spindles
85' - John Locicero (P)
Matchweek 2 was a special one for the club, as Spindles debuted the new White Away Kit by Icarus.
However, the beauty of the kits was not enough to prevent an ugly result for the Spins.
Spindles took on Highlanders, the same team the club dramtically defeated on Opening Night in 2022 and 2023.
But in 2024, Highlanders clearly wanted put end to that trend.
A beautiful night and great turnout at Nott Road, saw Spindles struggle to create clear chances.
Highlanders opened the scoring early within the first 15 minutes.
No matter what the Spins tried, the opposition shut it down.
A bleak first half left Spindles with nothing to lose in the second.
They entered the second half with more intensity, hoping to level the match.
However, a high line in attack left Spindles exposed yet again as Highlanders punished them, 2-0, 75'.
Despite a poor performace, Spindles still pushed for a site on goal.
Late in the match, John Locicero was brought down in the box and won a penalty which he calmly converted. 2-1, 85'.
But the push for goal was too little, and too late. Leaving Spindles with an early season blow.
The guys will have more than a week to bounce back and prepare for Rascals for Matchweek 3 on Thursday, May 23 at 8PM.

report.text: Rascals 2 - 0 Spindles
In the season's first Thursday night matchup, Spindles forgot to show up and were held scoreless against Rascals.
Two first-half goals and a dominant attacking threat left the Spins in the dust for the first 45'.
After a brief intermission, Spindles came out in the second half with much higher energy.
Moving the ball around, pressing the defense, and stopping attacks.
However, it was not enough as they struggled to complete a handful of chances.
Despite another great turnout of supporters, the Spins fell short with a final score of 2-0 Rascals.
This is now Spindles second straight loss, with 0 goals from open play across 180 minutes.
The players will have another week to flip the switch and look for all 3 points against Deathwish on Thursday, May 30 at 6:15 pm.

matches.reportTitle: Another Loss Haunts the Spins Early in the Season
matches.venueSource: CDSL league venue in club archives

report.text: Spindles 2 - 0 Deathwish
40' - John Locicero
64' - Ali Aladlouni (Ammar Singaporewala)
A clean sheet and a brace of goals was enough to secure all 3 points on Thursday for the Spins.
After two straight loses, the pressure was on to break that streak going into the early kickoff.
The Spins started the game with fire, creating chances and shutting down passes through the midfield.
Struggling to make that final pass into the attack.

Until nearly the end of the half, a Spindles corner saw Mason Kievit whip the ball onto the frame and as it was headed off the line. Luckily, John Locicero was there to finish it on the volley. 1 - 0, 40'.
Going into the second half with only a 1-goal lead, Spindles pressed to extend it.
20 minutes in, Ammar Singaporewala who dominated the midfield, pinged a ball out wide to Ali Aladlouni.
Aladlouni calmly settled the ball and chipped the keeper to get his first for Spindles. 2-0, 64'.
Some shaky moments saw Deathwish get a handful of chances in the first and second halfs.
But all the defenders on display came out to play, shutting down every opportunity and helping GK Ryan Taylor hold his first clean sheet.
A convincing win, but not enough on the attack from the Spins as they missed countless chances to rally the score.
Defensively, Singaporewala, and Captains Dan Crook and Cole Rust collectively earned the Man of the Match award, presented by Primeau's Autobody.
However, all 3 points go to Spindles, and they will look to build off this win in a rematch of last season's CDSL Final, on Tuesday, June 4 at 6:15pm vs. Vassi Realty.

matches.reportTitle: Getting Back to Winning Ways
matches.venueSource: CDSL league venue in club archives

report.text: Spindles 3 - 1 Vassi
12' - Ryan Breen (Mason Kievit)
19' - Ryan Breen
72' - Ali Aladlouni (Ethan Behan)
Another beautiful Tuesday evening at Nott Road was crowned with a near-perfect Spindles performance.
After 3 years in the CDSL, the Spins finally get all 3 points off 3-Peat Champions Vassi Realty.
Despite losing to Vassi in the final last season, it was clear that Spindles came to play this time.
Starting the match hot, forward Ryan Breen bagged his first this season within the first 15.
A run down the wing gave Mason Kievit a clear opening to play Breen in, leaving just him and the keeper to slot it past. 1-0, 12'.
The press continued for Spindles.
7 minutes after the opener, a corner kick saw a half volley from Luke Geczy hit the bottom of the crossbar.
Luckily, Breen was there to clean it up with a header for his second of the night. 2-0, 19'.
Spindles, pumped and determined, took a quick halftime break and picked up right where they left off in the second.
More press in the Vassi half gave Ethan Behan the opportunity to cross toward Ali Aladlouni.
After a slight deflection off the defender, Aladlouni took it off the volley and curled one in the top left.
The nearly 100 supporters in attendance roared. 3-0, 72'.
Although the attack showed up to finish chances, the defense truly saved the game on multiple occasions.
Goal-line clearances and last-second tackles help the Spins hold a strong lead all match.
The final score ended at 3-1. It is the first time Spindles United has ever beaten Vassi Realty.
Breen was named the Gent's Barber Co. Man of the Match for bagging his first 2 goals of the season.
Another massive thank you to all the supporters that came out. Your commitment is unparalleled.
Thank you to the boys from Rotterdam United SC for supporting their coaches, Mason and John!
We were proud to give our biggest supporter Aiden a win to remember, and a scarf to go along with it.
We will see y'all next week. Same time. Same place.

matches.venueSource: CDSL league venue in club archives

report.text: Collar City 2 - 0 Spindles
The Spins killed their chance to go 3 wins in a row on Tuesday night against Collar City FC.
After failing to finish several chances in the first 15, Collar City found the net for their first two chances of the match.
2-0 at halftime.
After another slow half in the second, Spindles failed to find the net once with several clear chances.
2-0 was the final score at Nott Road.
Not good enough from Spindles.
All eyes toward Saturday for the club's first-ever Grassroots Cup at Lansing Park.
We will see you there.

matches.reportTitle: The Spins Held Scoreless Again
matches.venueSource: CDSL league venue in club archives

report.text: Spindles 5 - 3 Highlanders
12' - Geczy (Rabadi)
25' - Behan (Crook)
36' - Rabadi (Rust)
50' - Adjei (Maguire)
52' - Geczy
The 2024 Grassroots Cup had no shortage of entertainment and excitement.
From the start of the event to the kickoff, to the goals, and to the celebrations.
More than 300 spectators packed Lansing Park on Saturday evening to watch Spindles United host Highlanders FC in the Spindles first home game.
Accompanied by a bouncy house, food, face painting, raffles, music, and beautiful weather.
From start to finish, the first-time event was a big success for the club.
The match kicked off with a typical walkout ceremony to announce the players headlining the match.
Imani Payne, a Cohoes resident of the Spindle City Vineyard was at the helm of the National Anthem.
Josie Parker and Mia Snyder stepped up at the announcer's table for the match.
The match scoring was opened early by Luke Geczy's header off of a Matt Rabadi set piece. 1-0, 12'.
However, Highlanders bounced right back to level the score at 1-1.
Luckily, Dan Crook leaped a cross from half field to find Ethan Behan at the 6' for a quick header over the keeper. 2-1, 25'.
As Spindles always does, they conceded shortly after scoring again to bring the game level again.
4 goals in the first 25 minutes.
And make that another one as Rabadi took his chance from kickoff at half field, and found the back of the net over the keeper. 3-2, 36'.

Going into the break, the event was at its peak. A full touchline of spectators, 5 goals, and goal music galore, and Riley Kean was putting in an extra shift when running the Spindles flag up and down the field.
At halftime, the club also got to announce the winner of the highly anticipated PS5 raffle.
Congratulations to Oliva Rust!
All the proceeds of the raffle go to the development of future Spindles youth programs.
Kicking off the second half in style, Zeidane Adjei awaited a corner kick by Ian Maguire before heading the cross in. Spindle's 3rd header of the match. 4-2, 50'
Shortly after, Luke Geczy had his eyes on second when he took a volley from outside the 18' to put it away in the bottom corner. 5-2, 52'.
The final score of the match was 5-3. An 8 goal thriller from both sides.
A big thank you to Highlanders for accepting our invitation to play.
We were grateful to have AKI Food Truck, Pizza Stop, & Cinnamon Breeze in attendance to give people some great food options.
A thank you to all the volunteers who helped on the day.

Jim Powers, Kennedy Bryant, Anna Winedecker, Josie Parker, Erin Parker, Mia Snyder, Megan LaPlante, Grace D'Angelo, Rayan Essoulaimani, Adam Essoulaimani, Ryan Frangie, Imani Payne, Andrew Li, Giovanni Lopriggo, Richard Kouacou, Joseph Casale and Riley Kean.
To the businesses and organizations that help with the donation of goods.
Admar Construction Equipment, B95.5/Pamal Broadcasting, Cohoes Recreational Soccer, the City of Cohoes, and Tech Valley Office Interiors.
Events like these are the reason why we started Spindles United FC.
It's not all about winning games, but mostly about community.
Holding this free community event at our home base was our way of showing who we are, and why we are here.
And we are not going anywhere. Up the Spins.

report.text: FCSB 3 - 0 Spindles
Our first match-up against the CDSL leaders FCSB was one to forget.
Mostly playing in the Spindles half, a strong defensive effort from the Spins wasn't enough to get a result.
Spindles soaked in the pressure for the first half, going into the break level at 0.
However, a few lapses in the middle and back thirds gave FCSB more clear-cut chances in the second half.
Of those chances, 3 of them were put away throughout the rest of the match.
Final score ended at 3-0, FCSB.
A hard-fought match leaves Spindles feeling motivated to finish off the regular season strong and salvage a strong playoff seeding.
We will see you next week at 6:15 pm vs. Ligon FC.

matches.reportTitle: Spindles Bested by the League Leaders
matches.venueSource: CDSL league venue in club archives

report.text: Spindles 1 - 0 Ligon FC
15' - Adjei (Aladlouni)
After 2 straight league losses, Spindles is finding their feet again with a win over Ligon FC.
Spindles took on last-place Ligon FC on Tuesday night, looking for all 3 points to help their playoff-seeding chances.
For another beautiful Nott Road night, all it took was 1 goal to seal the deal.
Zeidane Adjei opened the scoring early after a trivela cross by Ali Aladlouni, for an easy half-volley for Adjei. 1 - 0, 15'.
Spindles dominated possession and chances for the first and second halfs.
Although the opposing keeper made some great stops, Spindles will be disappointed not to have extended their lead this match.
A strong defensive performance from the Spins helped secure a clean sheet for the night, giving Ligon very few chances.
With that being said, centreback Ian Maguire earned the Guth DeConzo Man of the Match award for his stopping display.
Spindles are hoping for another 3 points next week, Tuesday, July 2 against Highlanders at 6:15 pm.

matches.reportTitle: Getting Back on Track with 3 Points
matches.venueSource: CDSL league venue in club archives

report.text: Spindles 3 - 2 Highlanders
5' - Adjei (Behan)
30' - Locicero (Buttofucco)
34' - Buttofucco
As the end of the regular season closes in, every point is crucial in the race for the best possible playoff seeding.
Tuesday night's victory over Highlanders was a big step for Spindles.
A strong first half was ultimately enough for the win.
Zeidane Adjei opened the scoring thanks to the pressure of Ethan Behan on a keeper error outside of the box.
Adjei chipped it in from 30 yards out, 1-0, 5'.
More chances rolled in for the Spins.
Later in the half, a low corner kick from Anthony Buttofucco found its way to John Locicero for an easy tap-in. 2-0, 30'.
With the momentum in Spindles favor, Buttofucco blew past 2 Highlanders defencemen down the wing and tucked one in the bottom right corner. 3-0, 34'.
Buttofucco's first goal for the club.
Feeling optimistic at the break, the second half became a tougher battle for Spindles.
Highlanders did not give up, pressing all half in the hope for a comeback.
A defensive error at the top of the box gave Highlanders a free shot to make the score 3-1.
With more pressure coming, Spindles conceded a penalty during the referee's stoppage time.
Luckily for the Spins, the spot kick was not enough. Settling the final score at 3-2.
A hard-fought 3 points as we enter the final matchweek of the regular season on Thursday, July 11 at 8 pm against Rascals.

matches.reportTitle: A Crucial Win in the Race for Playoffs
matches.venueSource: CDSL league venue in club archives

report.text: Spindles 5 - 1 Rascals
5' - Buttofucco (Crook)
43' - Locicero (Rabadi)
60' - Rabadi (P)
78' - Breen (Geczy)
88' - Lopez (Sanchez)
The Spins capped off the regular season with a massive win over Rascals.
Not only did the victory include 5 Spindles goals, but most importantly it was the result we needed to take the 2nd place seed for the CDSL playoffs.
After starting the week in 5th place, playoffs were guarantteed but only a point separated 5th and 2nd place.
Meaning it all to play for for 4 teams during the last couple of weeks.
With a bit of luck in other matches and 3 straight Spindles wins to end the season, the Spins secured 2nd.
CDSL Playoffs
In the CDSL there are 8 teams. At the end of the 10-game regular season, seeds 1 and 2 secure a bye-week and go straight to the semi-finals.
Meanwhile seed 3 plays 6 and seed 4 plays 5 in the quarterfinals next week.
In this case, the highest seed of those 2 matches to advance will face Spindles on Thursday, July 25 in the semi-finals.
Match Recap
The last time Spindles came up against Rascals was a Matchweek 3, 2-0 loss.
With the 2nd seed in site, winning was the only option this time around.
The scoring kicked off early when Dan Crook pinged a ball over the Rascals backline to Anthony Buttofucco, who touched it around the keeper and practicially dribbled it over the line. 1-0, 5'.
Shortly after, a lapse in the Spindles defence led to an easy Rascals goal. 1-1. A happy site for the opposing teams in attendance.

Luckily, before the end of the half Matt Rabadi broke the defensive line with a floating cross to John Locicero, who was able to bring it down and around the keeper before hammering it home. 2-1, 43'.
Locicero's 4th of the season, making him joint Spindles top-scorer with Zeidane Adjei headed into playoffs.
At halftime, the club hosted a FREE raffle for a Spindles Independence Day Trucker Hat made by our match sponsor Capital Region Embroidery.
Congrats to Russell Phoenix for winning the hat! A OG Spindles vet.
The second half went on to be just as eventful in the first.
The Spins continued to create chances.
15 minutes in, Rabadi came barreling down the wing before a Rascals defender stepped in too late, taking him out in the box. Penalty to Spindles.
Rabadi calmly converted it, 3-1, 60'.
The Spindles backline continued to shut down any Rascals chance before it even made their final 3rd.
Meanwhile, the attack was fully focused on extending the 2 goal lead.
Eventually, Luke Geczy played a perfect pass to Ryan Breen after some great hold up play.
Never in doubt when 1v1 with the keeper, Breen slotted it in the bottom left corner. 4-1, 78'.
A comfortable lead for the Spins.
With everyone trying to get on the scoresheet, Danny Sanchez shot up and down the wing while closing out the game.
After a late breakaway, Sanchez plays a perfectly weighted pass to Marcos Lopez who crushed one through the keepers hands and into the net. 5-1, 88'.
Lopez's first for the club.
A perfect ending to a regular season full of ups and down. But ultimatley became the clubs best regular season finish at 2nd place with 6 wins and 4 losses.
With the bye-week, the Spins will have plenty of time to rest and work to prepare for the semi-finals.
See y'all in the Y'offs.

matches.reportTitle: Closing Out the Regular Season in Style
matches.venueSource: CDSL league venue in club archives

report.text: Vassi 2 - 1 Spindles
65' - Piperata (Geczy)
On Thursday Night, the Spins had the chance to get to a second straight CDSL Final. However, the night did not quite go to plan.
Spindles United took on Vassi Realty in the Semi-Finals last week, a rematch of last year's final. The winner booked their spot in the CDSL Semi-Final on July 30.
Hopes and energy were high amongst the players and supporters going into the match.
Our previous meeting with Vassi came mid-season where the Spins won 3-1, the club's first time beating the 3-time champs.
In this edition, the game started back and forth with both teams finding chances. However, things quickly went south.

Just 10 minutes in, a Spindles defensive error led to a 1-on-1 chance for Vassi. Goalkeeper Ryan Taylor made the stop before a Vassi player followed up on the rebound. On the goal-line, defender Cole Rust stopped the shot with 2 hands. A straight red for Rust, and a penalty to Vassi.

The Vassi player stepped up confidently but managed to hit the bottom right post. He then followed the deflection up to bury it in the net, before the referee called no goal as the ball did not hit any other players before he hit it a second time.
0-0, 10'. Spindles down to 10 men for the rest of the match.

A gritty second half showed that Spindles was not out of it. After keeping the score level at 0 at the half, things were gearing up for an eventful second half. 10 minutes into the second, the high press by Vassi was too much, giving the champs the first lead of the night.
However, Spindles continued to connect, work, and create chances. Despite being down a man all game.

Soon after, Luke Geczy holds the ball perfectly at the midfield before sending Joe Piperata in on goal. His fake shot sends the defender to the shops, letting Pip calmly slot it through the keeper's legs, bringing Spindles level while down a man. 1-1, 65'.
More chances continued to pour on, allowing Spindles to dominate most of the second half. An even match with extra time in sight. Looks like it will be a late one.
However, a dominant performance was quickly shattered in the 89th minute.
A challenge at the edge of the box saw Vassi be awarded a penalty, ultimately deciding the game. The Spins lose 2-1 and head out of playoffs earlier than we hoped.
A heartbreaking result.
The players did everything they could to stay in a game that most teams would have given up in the 10th minute.
It was a true sign of the boy's effort and determination all season long, and we couldn't be prouder of their fight.
Seeing another great crowd come out to support that night, was a testament to all the things we look forward to achieving on and off the field.
Although our 2024 CDSL season is over, the work to build a community-based club will not be stopped.
Continue to follow us this summer and off-season as we prepare several exciting announcements for the future of Spindles.

The Spins returned to action last night against the reigning 2022 CDSL Champions, Vassi Realty.

Spindles came out in the second half looking to bring the match level. They continued to dominate possession but Vassi held things down defensively.

Eventually, Jaycen Janusz shot from the top of the box, hitting the Vassi defender's hand, and giving the Spins a penalty. New team captain Jad Essoulaimani converted and made it 1-1. His first of the season.
The battle continued, with some more good play by the Spins.
This led to a beautifully weighted through ball by Man of the Match winner Drew Michel to Ethan Behan to take the lead 2-1. The striker's first goal for the club.
Unfortunately, celebrations were short and within a minute Vassi countered and scored the tying goal. Which resulted in a 2-2 draw, rewarding both teams with 1 point.

report.text: Spindles 6 - 1 Backheel FC
7' - Drew Michel
9' - Jad Essoulaimani16' - Moulay Ahmed Aladlouni (Ethan Behan)40' - Zeidane Adjei (Drew Michel)
59' - Ethan Behan
80' - Reggie Esconde (Danny Sanchez)
After weeks of rescheduling due to Canadian Wildfires, Matchweek 5 against Backheel FC finally occurred last night at Nott Road.
It's safe to say it was worth the wait for Spindles United.

After weeks of struggling to start matches strong, the Spins changed that narrative early on this hot summer night. An opening goal 7 minutes in from a beautiful run down the wing by Drew Michel and tucked in the corner for the lead—his first of the season.
2 minutes later, Captain Jad Essoulaimani lifted one of his signature freekicks over the wall and past the keeper for 2-0.
By the 16', Moulay Ahmed Aladlouni extended the lead to 3 from a heading pass by Ethan Behan. Aladlouni's first of the season.
Just before the half, Michel blessed the crowd with another magical run down the stretch and perfectly served Zeidane Adjei for a quick 1-2 finish. His first of the season.
Backheel came out strong in the second half, however, the Spins continued to create chances.
In the 59', Behan netted his first of the match after a miscommunication in the opposition's defense, extending the lead to 5-0.

Reggie Esconde closed out the scoring in the 80' with a shot from no angle at the end line, catching the keeper off his line. Set up by a long pass by Danny Sanchez. Esconde's first of the season brought the Spins to a 6-0 lead.
A well-earned clean sheet by Jordan Prouty and his defense was taken in the 89', settling a final score of 6-1 Spindles.
With 1 goal and 1 assist, Michel was easily awarded the Man of the Match. Michel played a crucial role in both the attack and defense.
Although the win brought Spindles to the top of the league, there is no time to celebrate as they go back to work this Tuesday, June 27 at 8 PM to take on second-place Vassi Realty.

report.text: Spindles 2 - 1 Backheel
35' - Ryan Breen (Moulay Ahmed Aladlouni)
43' - Ben Kellis
With the sun shining in the Capital Region again, the Spins return to winning ways.
Sunday night's affair with Backheel FC was the first round of the 2023 CDSL Playoffs. Spindles (#3) and Backheel (#6) both came looking for a spot in the semi-finals.
The match was a battle between both sides.
The first half saw a handful of chances and heated play from both sides.
A dramatic night for the 80+ spectators who watched on.
Luckily, the Spins opened the scoring with a strong run from Moulay Ahmed Aladlouni down the wing for a touch to the middle for an easy finish for Ryan Breen, 35'. His second of the season.
Shortly after in the 43', Ben Kellis pressed the keeper with the ball at his feet, and forced an error that led to a deflected goal of Kellis for his first of the season and club career.
Confidence was high at the break. The Spins were hungry for more.
However, things quickly became shaky when the Spins gave up a penalty 3 minutes into the second half. A powered shot down the middle brought the Heels within 1.
Both sides pressed the rest of the match in search for another crucial goal.

Chance after chance left everyone wondering if this match was going to flip over on its head.With a 1 minute left, Backheel get a break and push it out wide to an unmarked forward , leaving him 1v1 with keeper Josh Marer.
Marer came up big making a diving save to push the ball wide, securing the Spins lead and saving their season.
The final whistle blew shortly after for a score of 2-1 Spindles.
Man of the Match was awarded to Jimmy Alexander.
Alexander controlled the game in the back, middle and final third for all 90 minutes.
As great as the win felt, the Spins knew that the job is far from done.
Spindles United (#3) will take on Deathwish (#2) this Thursday, July 27 at 8PM, Nott Road Park for a chance at a ticket to the final.

report.text: Spindles 4 - 2 Deathwish

Spindles United (3) took on Deathwish (2) in a CDSL Semi-Final clash on Tuesday night.
During the regular season, Deathwish bested the Spins twice. Outscoring the red 9-2 across two games. But the third time seemed the charm.
The first 30 minutes of the game was dominated by Spindles in possession and chances.
However, against the grain, Deathwish had their first chance with a counterattack to open the scoring, 1-0 30'.
That did not stop the Spins though.
Within minutes, a hard attacking press caused a turnover from Deathwish. Forward Zeidane Adjei capitalized by scoring a beautiful 20-yard curler into the top corner, 33'. His second of the season.
Shortly after in the 39', Adjei found himself in a similar position hitting another screamer. Putting the Spins up 2-1. Now his third of the season.
More pressure from Spindles lead to another defensive mistake on the Deathwish backline. Forward Luke Geczy capitalized and slotted his first goal of the season into the bottom corner, 44' 3-1.
The second half started with more fire, as the Spins found themselves in another attack with Moulay Ahmed Aladlouni serving Luke Geczy for his second of the match, 47' 4-1.
Last night's match was Geczy's first time back on the roster since Matchweek 6 due to a hamstring injury.
Spindles continued the second half with the majority of possession.
But the opposition did not back down.
Deathwish scored a late goal in the hopes of a comeback.
But the Spins back third held on strong with crucial saves from goalkeeper Josh Marer.
Man of the Match winner Capitan Cole Rust kept the defense organized and disciplined to hold off any more goals.
The match ended 4-2, punching a ticket for Spindles United's first-ever finals appearance.
Spindles United will take on the winner of Vassi Realty (1) vs. Rascals (5) in the last semi-final this Sunday.
The championship match will be held on Thursday, August 10 at 8:30 pm

report.text: Vassi 3 - 1 Spindles
66' - Jack Phillips (Ryan Breen)
In just their second year as a club, Spindles United took on CDSL giants Vassi Realty in the league final on Thursday night.
The wet summer of 2023 continued into Thursday night's final, leaving a wet, foggy, and humid event.
The match started strong for Vassi, who scored the opening goal 3 minutes in, 1-0.
As the fog continued to creep in, Vassi did not slow down looking to add to their lead with several dangerous chances.
Eventually, the Spins settled in and started creating ideas.
The rest of the first half was back and forth between both sides.
By the half, Vassi had a 1-0 lead with the Spins hungry to bounce back.
However this was shortly shot down after Vassi pushed forward straight off kickoff to make it 2-0 less than a minute into the second half, 45'.
Nott Road was silent.
However as the timer continued to tick away, the Spindles United record attendance crowd of 156 really made their presence heard.

By the 66' forward Ryan Breen found himself attacking the wing and setting up a weak footed cross into the box. Forwrd Jack Phillips was on the other end for a towering header over the defenders and past the keeper, 2-1. Phillips first goal for the club.
The crowd roared as the Spins scored their first finals goal in what looked like the beginning of a dramatic comeback.
However, the match continued to give chances to both sides, eventually leading to a 90' goal by Vassi to seal their 3rd CDSL Championship title in a row.
Spindles United finish second in the league, their highest finish since joining the CDSL last year.
What seemed to be a night to forget, actually became one to remember forever.
Almost 160 supporters packed Nott Road. Some drove great distances to see the Spins live on Thursday night.
It was clear that this final meant more than just winning silverware.
Instead it showed how far the greatest grassroots club in the world has come in just 2 years. And more importantly, how far it can go.
